Implementation Plan

Implementation plan for #6883: making a failed orchestrate-poll CI shard name its failing test

Planning ref: `main` @ `de45b6cf454f106c197dd3cc00a499324619ad6c` (symbolic branch `main`). The issue carries no integration-branch metadata, so there is no ref mismatch.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends the existing orchestrate-poll shard-judgment loop in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `mark-stable.yml` and `test-and-mark-stable.yml`, and its `run_shard_judge` harness in `tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py`
Scope-mode justification: The clarification answers set the scope: Q1:A, Q2:A and Q3:A. First, try to reproduce the shard-1 failure on `main` and fix it only if it reproduces there. Second, always add the diagnostic: a failed shard reports its own `FAIL` lines. Nothing else is in scope. No retries and no change to exit codes, because Q3:C would hide real failures. The three copies of the judgment loop are already kept identical and tested together by `ShardJudgeTest`, so the diagnostic goes into the same three loops. A new helper script would split the pattern the harness already tests, so the change stays inline. Doing all three copies costs only a few lines more than doing `ci.yml` alone. Per §6 (Correctness > Speed), the complete version wins and the three copies stay in step.

Automation / scheduler impact
- No new script and no new supervisor. Only existing workflow steps and one test file change.
- Entry points are unchanged: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` job `orchestrate-poll` (push / pull_request), and the `validate-scripts` jobs in `.github/workflows/mark-stable.yml` and `.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml`.
- No database work, no `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` entry, and no new env var.

1. Files likely to change
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: shard-judgment loop at about lines 1416-1443.
- `.github/workflows/mark-stable.yml`: same loop at about lines 371-397.
- `.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml`: same loop at about lines 4839-4865.
- `tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py`: new cases in `ShardJudgeTest`.
- `changelog.d/6883-orchestrate-poll-fail-annotations.md`: new fragment, `<!-- changelog: changed -->` (or `fixed` if step 1 fixes a real defect). Same structure as `changelog.d/6839-*.md`.
- Only if step 1 reproduces a failure on `main`: `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py` and/or `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`.

2. Functions / modules to implement

Step 1: try to reproduce on `main` (Q1:A, Q3:A)
- Run the module locally, split into 4 shards the same way the release gate does:
  - Derive the test names with the same AST command the release step uses.
  - Shard them with `awk -v n=<i> -v total=4 'NR % total == n'`.
  - Run each shard with `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py <names…>` in parallel.
- If any `  FAIL  ` line appears:
  - Re-run that test alone to confirm it fails consistently.
  - Fix the root cause in the test, or in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` only if the failure shows a poller defect.
  - Never loosen an assertion just to make it pass.
- If every shard passes:
  - Change no test or poller code.
  - Say in the PR body that the failure was on PR #6581's head (`a998d15`), does not reproduce on `main`, and is left to that PR's own review loop or was transient.
- If the run cannot finish in the time budget, mark reproduction UNVERIFIED in the PR body and continue with step 2.
- Context: `changelog.d/6839-merge-gate-ci-aggregate-check.md` records that `main` had red CI after PR #6643 until #6839. The shard-1 failure may have been inherited from that breakage. Mention this possibility in the PR body; do not assert it as the cause.

Step 2: the diagnostic, in all three workflows (Q2:A)

All edits go inside the judgment loop that starts at `shard_failures=0`:

a) Right after `shard_failures=0`, add two initialisers:
   - `fail_annotations=0`
   - `failed_test_lines=()`

   They must come after that marker so `run_shard_judge`, which slices from `shard_failures=0`, picks them up.

b) In the `if [ "${shard_rc}" -ne 0 ]` branch, after the existing two lines (the `failed (exit ...)` echo and the counter increment), which stay as they are:

   ```
   shard_fail_lines="$(LC_ALL=C awk '/^  FAIL  / && c < 20 { c++; line = substr($0, 3, 500); gsub(/%/, "%25", line); gsub(/\r/, "%0D", line); print line }' "/tmp/poll_shard_${shard}.log")"
   [ -n "${shard_fail_lines}" ] || shard_fail_lines="no FAIL line in log (runner or fixture error); see the shard log group"
   while IFS= read -r fail_line; do
     failed_test_lines+=("orchestrate-poll shard ${shard}: ${fail_line}")
     if [ "${fail_annotations}" -lt 5 ]; then
       echo "::error::orchestrate-poll shard ${shard}: ${fail_line}"
       fail_annotations=$((fail_annotations + 1))
     fi
   done <<< "${shard_fail_lines}"
   ```

   - The extraction is a single awk call. The obvious `grep | head` pipeline would fail under the runner's `-eo pipefail` when grep gets SIGPIPE.
   - Escaping covers `%` and `\r`. awk records never contain `\n`.
   - Multi-line failure messages contribute only their first line, which is the one starting with `  FAIL  `.
   - Each emitted line has the form `FAIL  <name>: <error>`.

c) In the final `if [ "${shard_failures}" -ne 0 ]` block, before the existing tally `echo`:

   ```
   if [ "${#failed_test_lines[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
     echo "orchestrate-poll failing tests:"
     printf '  %s\n' "${failed_test_lines[@]}"
   fi
   ```

   This plain-text list lands at the end of the job log, so a log tail (what triage reads) names every failed test, including any beyond the annotation cap.

d) Comment: one comment above the new block citing issue #6883 and run 37906796258, and explaining the annotation cap.

e) Leave the rest of the loop unchanged:
   - The no-log branch, since there is no log to read.
   - The `::group::` output.
   - The existing `::error::` lines: `produced no log; its tests did not run`, `failed (exit N)`, and `N orchestrate-poll shard(s) failed.`
   - `exit 1`.

3. Data structures affected
- Two new bash locals inside the judgment loop: `fail_annotations` (an integer) and `failed_test_lines` (an array).
- No state, labels, artefacts or schemas change.
- New variable names checked for clashes: none of `fail_annotations`, `failed_test_lines`, `shard_fail_lines` or `fail_line` appears in any of the three steps. The implementer should confirm with grep.

4. API / interface changes
- New annotations, all using the existing `orchestrate-poll shard <N>` prefix:
  - `::error::orchestrate-poll shard <N>: FAIL  <test>: <error>`
  - `::error::orchestrate-poll shard <N>: no FAIL line in log (runner or fixture error); see the shard log group`
- New plain-text block `orchestrate-poll failing tests:`.
- Existing log keys, exit codes and the `CI_POLL_TEST_SHARDS` interface are unchanged.

## Decisions

### D1 — Cap the new annotations at 5 per step, and list every failure in plain text
- Chosen:
  - At most 5 test-name `::error::` annotations per step, across all shards.
  - Up to 20 FAIL lines per shard are collected, and all of them are printed in a plain-text block just before the tally line.
- Alternatives considered: 20 annotations per shard, as the clarify-respond execution plan proposed.
- Why:
  - As I recall, GitHub keeps at most 10 error annotations per step and 50 per job. I did not verify this against current documentation.
  - With the default 4 shards all failing, the existing lines already use 5 (4 `failed (exit N)` plus 1 tally). A cap of 5 keeps the total at 10 or below, so no existing annotation is dropped.
  - The plain-text list still gives every name to log-tail readers such as triage.

### D2 — Keep the change inline in all three workflows instead of a shared helper script
- Chosen: duplicate about 15 lines in `ci.yml`, `mark-stable.yml` and `test-and-mark-stable.yml`.
- Alternatives considered: a new `scripts/ci_poll_shard_fail_annotations.sh` called from all three.
- Why:
  - The three loops are already kept as identical copies.
  - `run_shard_judge` runs the real step text, so inline code is tested as shipped.
  - A helper would add a new automation path and a dependency on how the release-gate checkouts stage `scripts/`.

### D3 — Escape the annotation text in awk, before echoing it
- Chosen: escape `%`→`%25` and `\r`→`%0D` inside the extraction awk.
- Alternatives considered: bash `${var//%/%25}` substitution.
- Why:
  - A leading `%` in a bash substitution pattern can be read as an end anchor, so `${var//%/%25}` may not replace every `%`.
  - awk `gsub` is unambiguous and also strips the leading two spaces and caps the length in one place.

## Security considerations
- Trust boundaries:
  - The annotation text comes from test output in `/tmp/poll_shard_*.log`.
  - On `pull_request` runs, that output comes from PR-head test code, the same code the step already executes and `cat`s into the log.
  - No new credentials and no new permissions.
- Injection:
  - Workflow commands are recognised only at the start of a line.
  - Every new line starts with a fixed `::error::orchestrate-poll shard <N>: ` or `orchestrate-poll shard <N>: ` prefix, so test text cannot start its own command.
  - `%` and `\r` are escaped in the annotation data, so a message cannot fake command parameters or split the line.
  - The existing raw `cat` of the log is unchanged. This change adds no new raw command surface.
- Secrets: the annotations repeat text already visible in the log, and GitHub masks registered secrets in annotations just as in
